prompt: An owl can turn its head around to about 270 degrees — far further than a human. Why does it need to do this?

options.text: Its ears are on the back of its head
Its eyes are fixed in their sockets and barely move
Its neck muscles are stronger than its wing muscles
It sleeps with its head facing backwards

explanation: Owl eyes are tube-shaped and fixed in their sockets, giving excellent vision but almost no eye movement — so the whole head must swivel instead.
